target.title: fix(ai): avoid websocket cache clobber on stale reused release
target.body:
Closes #105434

## What Problem This Solves
Releasing a reused ChatGPT Responses WebSocket deleted `websocketSessionCache` by session id without checking whether a newer same-session connection already owned that slot. A stale release could close/evict a valid replacement connection.

## Why This Change Was Made
The new-connection release path already guarded deletion with an identity check (`cache.get(sessionId) === entry`). The reused-lease release path and idle-expiry callback did not, so a replacement-before-release race could clobber the newer socket. This extends the same ownership guard to those async teardown paths.

## User Impact
Cached WebSocket sessions are less likely to drop a healthy replacement connection when an older reused lease later releases or expires. No config or API changes.

## Evidence
- Source: `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` reused `release` + `scheduleSessionWebSocketExpiry` now delete only when the cache still references the captured entry (mirrors the existing new-connection release guard).
- Test: added replacement-before-release coverage in `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`.
- Proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts` — 33 passed (Testbox warmup unavailable; local Vitest fallback).
- Autoreview: blocked in this environment (`codex` executable not found after secret-clean bundle prep).
